new_research_question: Can depth available only in an archived training pool help select which animal groups to annotate, reducing annotation cost for a final RGB-only BCS predictor? This tests annotation efficiency, not a claim to improve full-data RGB accuracy.
motivation: Direct distillation and feature-transfer candidates did not show reliable gains. Change the role of depth from teacher targets to training-pool acquisition information, and account explicitly for repeated observations and label cost.
budget_unit: Number of training episode labels; querying an animal group reveals all of its archived episode labels and costs that group's episode count. No acquisition may exceed the nominal episode-label budget. Validation labels are fixed and included in every reported total annotation cost.
initialisation: Same random animal-group order for every policy within a fold/seed, acquire three groups that fit within the first budget; no class-based initialisation or unqueried BCS balancing
features: Unchanged frozen DINOv2 global descriptors, no BCS fine tuning; RGB-only final predictor. The unlabeled training pool is available for feature distances; test/validation images do not define pool bandwidths or acquisition scores.
regressor: RBF SVR; gamma bandwidth uses full unlabeled training-pool median squared distance times [.5,1,2]; C=1/alpha with alpha [.01,.1,1,10], epsilon=.1. Retune with currently acquired labels plus fixed validation labels at each round, never with unqueried labels.
acquisition: For each eligible unlabelled group, average absolute RGB/depth prediction disagreement over its episodes. Multiply (0.25+0.75 percentile rank of disagreement) by (0.25+0.75 percentile rank of minimum joint-feature distance to acquired episodes), divided by square root of group label cost. Disagreement is refreshed once per batch; diversity is updated after each group in that batch.
committee_control: Ten group-bootstrap RGB SVRs at the selected RGB hyperparameters; prediction standard deviation replaces cross-modal disagreement, otherwise identical diversity/cost rule
core_set: Farthest group, using minimum episode distance to any acquired episode; divide by sqrt(group episode cost); RGB and RGBD representations tested separately
shuffled_control: Reassign the unlabeled depth predictions within the training pool by fixed random permutation before constructing disagreement; keep regression and queried true labels unchanged
primary_endpoint: Area under native-score MAE versus total annotation-cost fraction over [0.5,1.0], divided by 0.5; include the full fixed validation-label cost. Interpolate between actually achieved budget points, do not force curves to be monotonic.
secondary: MAE, animal-mean MAE, per-grade errors, actual episode labels, acquired animal groups, and grade representation at each budget; all six policies and ten seeds retained
test_evaluation: Freeze every acquisition trajectory and prediction before computing or printing test errors
scope: Retrospective simulation on previously scored archive; group metadata assumed available; counts of episode labels are a reproducible cost proxy, not measured veterinary minutes. Active privileged learning already exists; no first-general-method claim.
